An attempt to describe the state of the package, and to use what is there for providing
wrapper functions for ease of use ...

```{r setup}
library(nswtheme)
```

## Core colour palettes

- `col_nsw.R` has the **reference colour vector** and generates the "colour 
environment" `nsw_colour_grids` with named colour grids. These colour grids a referenced
by row and column to give a colour vector.

- `pal_nsw.R` generates the colour environment `nsw_named_palettes`, with each
named element a colour vector

```{r}
names(nsw_colour_grids)
nsw_colour_grids$base
nsw_colour_grids$aboriginal
nsw_colour_grids$corporate
nsw_colour_grids$treasury
```

```{r}
names(nsw_named_palettes)
nsw_named_palettes$default
nsw_named_palettes$core
```

`utils-display_pal_nsw.R` provides the function `display_pal_nsw()` to display features
described above

```{r}
display_pal_nsw()
```

`col_nsw()` picks colours from `nsw_colour_grids` and produces a vector

```{r}
col_nsw(variant = 'base', tone = 'normal')
col_nsw(variant = 'aboriginal', tone = 'normal')
```

`pal_nsw()` generates a colour function from all of the above (with the maximum
number of available colour being the length of the colour vector (core = 2 colours).
You must distinguish between **palette** and **variant** - TODO!

```{r}
# pal_nsw -> get(palette, envir = nsw_named_palettes)

pal_nsw(palette = 'core')(2) # same as nsw_named_palettes$core
pal_nsw(variant = 'base', tone = 'normal')(10) # same as col_nsw(variant = 'base', tone = 'normal')
```

> ggplot2 often takes in colour functions .. therefore use pal_nsw


nsw_theme() is a `ggplot2` theme with these colour defaults:

```
theme(
  ...
  palette.colour.discrete = pal_nsw('default'),
  palette.fill.discrete = pal_nsw('default'),
  palette.colour.continuous = pal_nsw('default'),
  palette.fill.continuous = pal_nsw('default'),
  ...
  )
```

```{r}
pal_nsw(variant = 'base')
pal_nsw('default')(8)

```

all good until a beginner need use .. so some wrappers for scale_nsw_* defaults

```
scale_fill_nsw default
scale_fill_nsw aborignal etc
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

df <-
  data.frame(
    x = letters[1:4],
    y = rpois(4, 4)
  ) 

# This sets default colour + scales
set_theme(theme_nsw())

df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_col() 

df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = x)) +
  geom_col() 

# Shaun: Added
set_theme(theme_nsw(palette = 'treasury'))

df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_col()

df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = x)) +
  geom_col() 

# If you dont set themes
set_theme()

df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_col(fill = pal_nsw(variant = 'treasury', tone = 'normal')(1))

df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, fill = x)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_treasury()


```
